history: covid-rsv-coverage-20261118 (18-20 Nov) selected COVID T.pN_gru.real.log_loss1 + T.pN_gru.real + S.Ah.gru_national.real and RSV A4c0.national.rsvnet.calendar.weeks1 (+ .calendar), never submitted. The flu search (20-23 Nov) dropped both and found, on held-out 2024-25 and 2025-26 plus a 2023-24 guard: newest-week masking in training (newest_mask=0.1) -4.2% log-admission WIS for the mixture and -5.3% with a missing newest week; a sampled head with log-loss weight 1 on the B family; peak loss on sampled A-family recipes. problems.main: problems/us-{covid,rsv}-short-term-coverage.json: 2024-25 and 2025-26 each held out in turn, training on the other seasons of 2022-23..2025-26 (the 2024-25 fold also trains on the later 2025-26), labels = finalized future values (as of 12 Nov 2026), evaluated on the held-out season's archived Wednesday reports (finalized values where nothing was archived). For RSV the admission training data are 2024-25 and 2025-26 only (earlier weeks unobserved); ED share covers every season.
problems.guard: problems/us-{covid,rsv}-2023-24-prescribed-coverage.json (new, 24 Nov): 2023-24 held out, training on 2022-23, 2024-25 and 2025-26, evaluated on artificial preliminary 2023-24 reports (2025-26 reporting errors on admissions, ED and covariates, 3 draws). A third epidemic never used to select COVID/RSV models in the coverage search. For RSV it scores ED share only (no 2023-24 admissions in the RSV panel); for COVID, log admissions and ED share.

leak_free_errors: Main recipes carry no error_reference: each fold draws artificial reporting errors and real report pairs from its own latest training season (2024-25 for the 2025-26 fold, 2025-26 for the 2024-25 fold). Guard recipes carry error_reference=2025-2026 (required by the prescribed problem). Every recipe carries stress_views=1 (also scored with every location's newest admission week missing: view 'delayed'), an evaluation-only option. Scores are not comparable with covid-rsv-coverage-20261118.

families.covid ref: Production covid-gru-four members, leak-free: ref.Ah (width-192 sampled MLP, neighbouring states, network on corrected histories, errors on half the episodes), ref.pN (width-256 GRU direct-quantile, US-only summary, uncorrected artificial histories + final-value labels of the last 4 weeks, errors on 25% of episodes), ref.N (finalized histories, multiscale features, quantile), ref.Bh (width-256 MLP quantile, neighbours, weight decay).
families.covid 20 Nov: T = ref.pN with trees learned from real archived report -> value 12 weeks later pairs; Tl = T with log-loss weight 1; S = ref.Ah with GRU encoder, US-only summary and real-pair trees (sampled).
families.rsv ref: Production rsv-four members, leak-free: ref.Ball (width-512 quantile, neighbours, all six pathogen histories, trained on actual archived reports), ref.Bw (width-256 quantile, all six histories), ref.A4c0 (width-192 sampled MLP, corrected histories, Kinsa, no calendar), ref.A4i (A4 with all six histories, Kinsa).
families.rsv 20 Nov: Rc = A4c0.national.rsvnet.calendar (sampled MLP, US-only summary, Kinsa + RSV-NET rates, calendar, coverage signals in the error model); R1 = Rc correcting only the newest reported week.
families.children: One change each (rounds.py): nm10 (newest-week masking 0.1, the flu adoption), smp (sampled head on a quantile recipe), peak (peak loss on a sampled recipe), real (real-pair trees), cov (hospital coverage read by trees and network), ww (NWSS wastewater), nrevss (RSV lab positivity), esall (errors and pairs from every archived season), nokinsa, Bwq/Bwq.smp (RSV analogue of flu's Bq / Bq.smp.ll1).

selection_score: Primary: mean WIS of log(1 + admissions) over the 50 states and DC, Hub horizons 0-3, October-May reference dates, 2024-25 and 2025-26 equal (main problem), each recipe's deployed view ('corrected'), averaged over seeds; lower is better. Reported beside it: each season, the 2023-24 guard (COVID log admissions; RSV ED share x 1e4), October-only, US, ED share x 1e4 (both seasons), interval coverage, the 'delayed' stress view, pairwise relative WIS against the Hub models (scripts/flu_search_table.py --pathogen covid|rsv).
anti_overfitting_rules: No 2026-27 data in any training, evaluation or selection step (no live gate).
Eight seeds per recipe from the first screen (44-51); finalists get at least 8 more seeds (52-59) before any choice.

A child beats its parent only if its primary is lower by more than max(2 x standard error of the difference of seed means, 1% of the parent), it is lower in both 2024-25 and 2025-26, and its 2023-24 guard is not worse by more than that margin (RSV: ED share, same margin in percent). Smaller differences are 'level' and are not pursued.
Prefer changes with a mechanism (nowcast, double counting, data, structure) over continuous tuning; no random hyperparameter searches.
An axis is closed after two rounds without a 'better' child. Combinations only of children that were 'better' on their own.
The release candidate is chosen on seed mixtures of a few recipes, compared with the production mixture refit leak-free on the same seeds; mixture weights are equal, never tuned.

WIS in each state's peak window (target weeks within 2 weeks of its finalized season maximum) is reported for every finalist and mixture (scripts/flu_phase_check.py); a candidate may not be worse there by more than the margin.
